risk_if_not_implemented: Without Use of Third-Party Devices, supplier and External Service Provider (ESP) weaknesses, incidents or failures may propagate into the organization's environment unmanaged. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Access (R-AC-4), System / Data Compromise (Technical Vector) (R-BC-4), Uncontrolled Third-Party Security / Privacy Exposure (R-GV-5), Third-Party Cybersecurity Compromise / Exposure (R-SC-1), Loss of Confidentiality (R-IP-2), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Human Error (MT-9), Technical / Mechanical Failure (MT-10).

compensating_control_1.name: Third-Party Personnel Security
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to control personnel security requirements including security roles and responsibilities for third-party providers.
compensating_control_1.justification: Third-Party Personnel Security (TPM-13) provides third-party oversight that compensates for the absence of Use of Third-Party Devices (AST-26) by extending security obligations contractually and monitoring third-party risk in lieu of direct control. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Identification & Authentication for Non-Organizational Users
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to uniquely identify and centrally Authenticate, Authorize and Audit (AAA) third-party users and processes that provide services to the organization.
compensating_control_2.justification: Identification & Authentication for Non-Organizational Users (IAC-33) provides access control enforcement that compensates for the absence of Use of Third-Party Devices (AST-26) by restricting system and data access to authorized users through alternative identity and access mechanisms. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
